trees.title: Vibration in the car
trees.summary: You feel vibration in the steering wheel, in the brake pedal, or through the whole car.
trees.safety: A bulge in the tyre sidewall, or strong vibration that worsens with speed, are a reason not to drive fast until you've checked — a tyre with a bulge can burst without warning.

n1.q: When do you feel the vibration?

options.label: In the steering wheel, at a certain speed, on a straight road
In the brake pedal, when braking
Through the whole car, when stationary with the engine running

n2.q: Does the vibration appear at roughly a fixed speed, and disappear when you speed up or slow down from it?

options.label: Yes, tied to a certain speed
No, it gradually worsens with speed, without a particular range

n3.q: Check the tyres — is there uneven wear or a bulge in the sidewall?

options.label: Yes, you see uneven wear or a bulge

n4.q: Is the vibration also accompanied by a knocking noise when you turn sharply?

options.label: No, just smooth vibration that worsens with speed

r-warped-disc2.text: Vibration or pulsing felt in the brake pedal, mainly when braking from high speed, points to a brake disc that has warped or worn unevenly.
actions: Go to a garage for a check, and to have the disc skimmed or replaced.
Until it's repaired, leave a bigger braking gap.

r-engine-mount.text: Vibration felt through the whole car when stationary with the engine running, which disappears once you drive, hints at a worn engine mount — the support that holds the engine and absorbs its vibrations.
actions: Go to a garage for a check and replacement.
A completely broken mount can let the engine move and damage the hoses and cables around it.

r-cv-joint-vibration.text: Vibration or a knock felt only in a sharp turn, mainly pulling into a parking space, points to a worn CV joint — mainly in front-wheel-drive cars.
actions: Go to a garage soon; a joint that fails completely can leave the car unable to drive.
Avoid sharp, fast turns until it's checked.

r-wheel-balance.text: Vibration that appears at roughly a fixed speed, and disappears when you speed up or slow down from it, is almost always an unbalanced wheel — balance weights that have fallen off, or a tyre fitted without balancing.
actions: Go to a tyre garage for wheel balancing — a quick and relatively cheap fix.
If the vibration continues even after balancing, check the rim and tyre for damage.

r-tyre-damage.result: Suspected tyre damage — uneven wear or a bulge
r-tyre-damage.text: Uneven wear or a bulge (bubble) in the tyre sidewall is a sign of structural damage in the tyre itself — a bulge in the sidewall can burst without warning.
actions: If you see a bulge in the tyre sidewall, don't drive on it, and change to the spare wheel.
Uneven wear alone, without a bulge — go to a garage to check the tyre and also the wheel alignment, since it's usually a result of that.

r-bent-rim.text: Vibration that gradually worsens with speed, without a particular range, and without a noise when turning, can indicate a wheel rim that has bent — for example after a hard hit in a pothole.
actions: Go to a tyre garage to check the rim's roundness.
Don't keep driving at high speed until it's checked.
